title: Vocabulaire Français Abloulé par M. Hucquart. Grand Bassam
evidence: BnF notice: 'Vocabulaire Français Abloulé ... Grand Bassam. 15 février 1850 ... Français et abouré.' From the Schoelcher bequest.
novelty_basis: Web search for Hucquart/Hecquard + abouré found nothing; Glottolog Abure page lists only modern refs. 'Hucquart' is probably Hyacinthe Hecquard, who was at Grand-Bassam c.1849-50 (my identification, not checked against sources).
language_status: well documented today; no other pre-1850s Abure lists known to me
notes: The images I sampled (f5, f9, f13, plus low-res thumbnails) came from the microfilm copy and looked blank or very faint, so I could not read any entries. Dated Feb 1850, just inside the cutoff.

title: Vocabulaire françois, anglois, portugais de l'Inde, persan, maure et bengale ... fait par moi Aussant, à Chandernagore, l'an 1782
language_as_named: portugais de l'Inde, persan, maure, bengale
modern_id: Indo-Portuguese creole (Bengal) [Glottolog: Indo-Portuguese]; Hindustani (moor1238? 'Moors'); Bengali (beng1280); Persian
size: 196 pp., 3700-3800 words, 6 columns, arranged by subject
evidence: Title page per BnF record: 'contenant 3700 à 3800 mots ... Vocabulaire sur 6 colonnes et distribué par matières.'
novelty_basis: Web searches for Aussant + Chandernagore 1782 vocabulary found nothing. Bengal Indo-Portuguese is very thinly documented; known items include Assumpção 1743 and SOAS MS 11952.
language_status: Bengal Indo-Portuguese extinct and thinly documented
notes: Gallica dates it 1801-1900 (probably the copy); the title page says 1782. I relied on the catalogue record and did not view the pages. If the Indo-Portuguese column is substantial this could be a major source for Bengal creole Portuguese.

title: Petit dictionnaire de la langue des Iroquois de la nation d'Agnié
evidence: Alphabetical French-Mohawk dictionary; begins 'Aage ...'; a note on f.1v says it is in the hand of the marquis de La Galissonnière.
novelty_basis: Web search turned up no study of it. Not checked in Pilling (probably listed there, since it is a BnF manuscript).
language_status: Mohawk well documented; 18th-c. French-Mohawk material is less so
notes: The attribution to the governor of New France (1747-49) is interesting.

title: Lempfrit, Dictionnaire du jargon Tchinouk; Dictionnaire de la langue Caoutchin
evidence: BnF record: title leaf reads 'Dictionnaire du Jargon Tchinouk 1849'; two-column vocabulary at ff.31-39.
novelty_basis: Edited in a long series on chinookjargon.com by D. Robertson, 2021-25 ('Lempfrit's legendary, long-lost linguistic legacy').
language_status: Chinook Jargon is a pidgin; the 1849 Cowichan list is early
notes: The Cowichan section may have had less attention than the Chinook Jargon part.

title: Dictionnaire des langues françoise et negres ... Compagnie Royale du Senegal (Guiolof, Foule, Mandingue, Saracolé, Seraire, Bagnon, Floupe...)
language_as_named: Guiolof, Foule, Mandingue, Saracolé, Seraire, Bagnon, Floupe
modern_id: Wolof, Pulaar, Mandinka, Soninke, Serer, Baïnouk, Jola
novelty_basis: BnF note says it was published in 1845 by the Société ethnologique (the printed 'Vocabulaires guiolof, mandingue...' is in Gallica as bd6t53581056).
language_status: Baïnouk and Jola sections are early
notes: Papel, Biafada ('Biragots'), Nalu and Sapi are named in the title, but the folio breakdown lists only seven languages. Worth checking whether those four sections exist and were left out of the 1845 edition.
